paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens for the baseline Mistral-v0.2-Base model and its variants fine-tuned on six different medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The horizontal axis, labeled "Per-specialty terms," lists these six specialties, each corresponding to a group of bars. The vertical axis, labeled "Negative log probability," is scaled linearly from -22 to -27, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Within each specialty group, there are seven bars: the leftmost bar (light blue) represents the baseline Mistral-v0.2-Base model, while the six adjacent bars (in shades of orange and brown) represent the same model fine-tuned on each of the six specialties, as indicated by the legend. The legend specifies that the fine-tuned models are color-coded as follows: light orange for Cardio, peach for Gastro, orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, brown for Obstetrics, and dark brown for Pediatrics. For each specialty group, the baseline model (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log-probability (lowest value on the y-axis, i.e., most negative), indicating lower likelihood of generating relevant tokens for that specialty. In contrast, the fine-tuned models exhibit lower negative log-probabilities (higher values on the y-axis, i.e., less negative), suggesting improved performance in generating specialty-specific tokens. Notably, the fine-tuned model for the same specialty (e.g., the "Cardio" fine-tuned model within the "Cardio" group) typically shows the lowest negative log-probability (highest value on the y-axis), indicating the best performance for that specialty. The bars are arranged in groups corresponding to the specialty being evaluated, and within each group, the fine-tuned models are ordered according to the legend, from Cardio to Pediatrics. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning on a specific specialty improves the model’s ability to generate relevant tokens for that specialty, with the most significant improvement observed when the model is fine-tuned on the same specialty as the evaluation set.
